calls.title: One docs PR into main, with 0.5.0 development work marked on the page
calls.chose: Trace every page against main (0.4.0) and dev/0.5.0, describe 0.4.0 as the baseline, and badge 0.5.0-only behaviour as development work; land it on main so the live site and GitHub's README update now
calls.because: The live site and GitHub front page both read main; 0.4.0 is the build people download; 0.5.0 is what Parker runs daily and ships Nov 20. One source with badges avoids tracing twice and keeps dev's docsite changes from being stranded
passed_over: PR into dev/0.5.0 only (live site stays 5 weeks stale until Nov 20)
Two layered PRs, 0.4 on main then 0.5 on dev (double tracing)
calls.undo: Revert the merge on main and redeploy; the badges can be deleted when 0.5.0 ships

reasons: both readings are medium under a standard posture

calls.title: Deploy the rebuilt docs site after the PR merges
calls.chose: Run docsite/deploy.sh from main once the PR is green and merged, after a dry run
calls.because: Parker asked for the docs WEBSITE to be updated; a push does not deploy; every 0.5.0 page and section says on its face that it is development work
passed_over: Leave the live site untouched (asks Parker to deploy by hand)
calls.undo: Re-run deploy.sh from the previous main commit; the site holds only this build

calls.title: docs/features becomes a map to the docs site
calls.chose: Replace each stale docs/features page with a short pointer to the docs-site page that was traced to code, keeping filenames so inbound links work, as issue 803 proposes
calls.because: Issue 803 found dozens of contradictions there; maintaining two copies is how they drifted; the site is the traced source
passed_over: Rewrite all 13 feature pages in place (a second copy to drift)
calls.undo: git revert restores the old pages
